task.description: Size ISS-0469 (executor_test.exs:654 raw wall-clock comparison, unguarded by :lua_wallclock_race, flaked 440ms vs 398ms on identical-commit CI reruns) and choose among its own 3 laid-out options -- (a) tag+isolate per ISS-0426 precedent, (b) deterministic proxy, (c) tolerance margin -- or route to CODE-DESIGNER if the choice needs real design invention.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause confirmed by reading the actual failing assertion and its surrounding test, not just re-quoting the issue's prose
Determined whether a deterministic proxy is readily available from data the Lua executor already exposes, or would require new design work
A real judgment call made among the viable options, with reasoning, not a bare enumeration
Routed to CODE-DESIGNER (if real design work is needed) or ELIXIR-DEV (if mechanical)

result.summary:
ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by reading executor_test.exs:625-658 in full, not just the issue's prose): the flaky assertion at line 654 (`assert small_elapsed_ms < large_elapsed_ms`) is REDUNDANT, not load-bearing. The test 'AC-1: a smaller configured max_heap_words halts sooner than a larger one on the same allocating script' already asserts, at lines 648-649, the fully deterministic outcome pair: `assert {:error, :memory_limit_exceeded} = small_result` and `assert {:ok, %{manifest_hash: _}} = large_result`, on the SAME allocating script under two different configured max_heap_words values. That pair alone already proves the configured limit is load-bearing (small limit kills the script; a materially larger limit lets the identical script complete) -- which is the entire substance AC-1 needs. The wall-clock `:timer.tc` comparison at 651-657 adds no additional proof of that property; it just re-measures the same two already-differently-outcomed calls in raw milliseconds and asserts on a margin (observed 440.152ms vs 398.195ms, ~10% -- well within ordinary CI scheduler-contention noise, and independently corroborated by ISS-0446 hitting the identical file:line on a prior, unrelated PR #866, i.e. this is a repeat offender, not a one-off).

CRUCIALLY, this redundancy is not incidental -- the test's own governing spec, test/specs/REQ-156.md T1 (lines 11-25), explicitly offers the outcome-based approach as an accepted, arguably PREFERRED alternative to a pure timing comparison: 'The test quotes real mix test output showing both calls' outcomes and relative timing (OR the larger-limit call's outcome differing from the smaller-limit call's ... IF THAT IS THE MORE RELIABLE WAY to demonstrate the limit is load-bearing rather than a no-op).' The test as written already does the outcome-differs half (satisfying T1/AC-1 on its own) AND additionally, unnecessarily, does the timing half too -- so the flaky half can be removed without losing any coverage the spec requires, because the spec itself names the surviving half as an acceptable, more-reliable substitute.

OPTION (b) DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, not just 'not readily available': I checked whether the executor already exposes a deterministic proxy (instruction count, checkpoint counter) that could replace the wall-clock comparison while proving the SAME property. It does expose `instruction_count` (lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex ~line 275-292, 488-492, off `Lua.VM.State`) -- but that counter belongs to the UNRELATED :max_instructions in-band budget mechanism (REQ-154), not to :max_heap_words. The module's own moduledoc (lines 123-127) explicitly documents this as a REJECTED design choice already on record (decision 0014's OQ-1): '`:max_instructions` is rejected as a memory-limit proxy ... allocation is not proportional to instruction count.' The max_heap_size kill path (lines 530-563) is an async BEAM-level `:erlang.spawn_opt` kill with `max_heap_size: %{kill: true}` -- it exposes no in-band counter of 'how much was allocated when killed' at all; the ONLY observable signal from that path is the return value itself (`{:error, :memory_limit_exceeded}` vs `{:ok, _}`), which the test already asserts on. Building a genuine word-count/checkpoint proxy would mean adding new instrumentation to a security-relevant kill path against an already-recorded decision-record preference not to couple the two mechanisms -- real design work, not a mechanical test edit, and not obviously worth it when the outcome assertions already prove the property per spec.

OPTIONS (a) AND (c) REJECTED AS WORSE THAN JUST DELETING THE REDUNDANT ASSERTION: (a) tag+isolate (ISS-0426 precedent, test_helper.exs's :lua_wallclock_race exclusion + lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex's isolated subprocess) is a clean mechanical fit, but it would grow the isolated-subprocess partition (already 11 tests per ISS-0426's own closure count) to cover an assertion that, per the spec, need not exist at all -- paying an isolation-and-maintenance cost for zero net coverage gain, and adding pattern debt the issue's own text already flags as a downside. (c) a tolerance margin keeps a wall-clock dependency and a hardcoded magic number that could still flake under sufficiently bad CI contention (this file:line has now flaked twice, per ISS-0446 and this issue) -- it treats the symptom, not the redundancy that is the actual root cause.

JUDGMENT: neither (a), (b), nor (c) as literally stated is the best fix. The correct fix is a 4th, narrower option the issue's framing did not need to anticipate because it falls out directly from re-reading the test against its own spec: DELETE the wall-clock measurement and comparison (the `:timer.tc` wrapping at lines 628-646 and the `small_elapsed_ms`/`large_elapsed_ms`/assert block at lines 651-657), keeping the two `Executor.run_with_heap_limit_sync/4` calls and their existing deterministic outcome assertions (lines 648-649) unchanged, and update the test's docstring/name (currently 'halts sooner than a larger one') to describe the outcome-differs property instead of a timing property (e.g. 'a smaller configured max_heap_words halts the script; a materially larger one lets the same script complete', matching test/specs/REQ-156.md's own alternative phrasing). This is mechanical -- deleting already-redundant lines and adjusting a test name/comment to match spec-sanctioned wording -- not a new design decision, so it does not need CODE-DESIGNER. No production code changes; scope is entirely inside the one test in test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs (lines 611-658, the AC-1 test and its preceding comment block).

Rename the test description from '...halts sooner than a larger one...' to an outcome-differs framing consistent with test/specs/REQ-156.md T1's own accepted alternative wording, and update the preceding comment block (lines 611-624) to state plainly that the timing comparison was removed as redundant with the outcome assertions (cite ISS-0469, and ISS-0446 as the prior corroborating flake) rather than isolated per ISS-0426, since the property no longer depends on wall-clock time at all. Run mix test against this one test file to confirm it still passes and no other test in the file references small_elapsed_ms/large_elapsed_ms.
